   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 22, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:57 p.m.
on Tuesday, November 22, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Herrera.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Jacqueline Borja, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto Jorge Herrera,
  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez and Riaz (Rick) Khan

Commissioners Absent:  Michelle Brenhaug

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 22, 2022
   3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Vice Chair Goto made some minor corrections for the October meeting minutes.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goto and seconded by Commissioner
  Fitzsimmons to approve the updated minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular
  Meeting for October 25, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0-1 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Brenhaug

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. REVIEW OF THE DRAFT NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH VIDEO
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez and Manager Morales Stevens presented the item.

  The Commission thanked staff for putting the video together. Commissioners
  enjoyed the video; they said it was emotional and showed the Chiefs’ passion.
  They discussed ways that this history can be shared with the community, such as
  a live museum with QR codes on city landmarks to provide information. The
  Commission thinks it would be great to have students gather the data and work
  with the tribal leaders for accurateness.

  B. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez presented the item.

  The Commission recapped this year’s accomplishments:
  • Implicit Bias Training for city employees
  • Mental Wellness Expo
  • Native American Heritage Video
  • Guest Speakers from various groups
  • Working towards Youth Ambassador program
  • Engagement Survey
  • Development of Land Acknowledgment Statement Advisory Committee

  Public Comment: None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 22, 2022
   C. DEVELOPMENT OF 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez presented the item
  The Commission suggests referring to survey results for suggestions from the
  community, responses included a multicultural event, playgrounds that are
  accessible for all children and LGBTQIA+ community support.

  The Commission would like to put together a Community Service project so that
  community members can collaborate and get to know each other.

  The Commission wants to dive deeper into Native American Heritage.

  The Commission wants to include an emphasis on senior protection and host a
  seminar educating senior citizens on fraud and scammers.

  The Commission wants to continue the Implicit Bias training for employees and
  continue partnership with Community Services Commission and Historic
  Preservation Commission and complete Land Acknowledgement Statement. They
  would like to follow up on the data collection from the city’s police department.
  They also requested to have more information on the city website that provides
  information on the Commission and what they do.

  Commissioners discussed ways to involve the youth in the Commission meetings.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Herrera attended the city’s Turkey Trot event.

  Vice Chair Goto attended the San Gabriel Valley Roundtable on Anti-Asian Hate
  co-hosted by Assemblymember Mike Fong and Attorney General Rob Banta. She
  shared that Asian Americans Advancing Justice Organization will host a one-hour
  virtual bystander training on December 14. She also mentioned that the Chinatown
  Service Center called out the need for cultural competency for law enforcement.
  She shared that the Japanese American National Museum is offering a free
  program on Saturday, January 21 called Bringing an American Vocabulary Words
  to Action into the Classroom. In honor of Native American Heritage Month, she
  invites everyone to join a live stream celebration hosted by Lakota People Law’s
  Project Virtual Wopila Gathering on November 29th.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez participated in the city’s Turkey Trot. She wanted to
  acknowledge the Public Works Department for the lighting in the Mission District.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 22, 2022
   She shared there will be the first Los Angeles Pow Wow event at Grand Park in Los
  Angeles organized by United American Indian Involvement, Inc. and Hilda L. Solis’
  office on December 3. She invited the community to attend the upcoming Holiday
  Tree Lighting. For the new year, she encourages everyone to gain personal
  connections with people that may be different from you.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS
  No staff comments.

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:12 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is scheduled in person for Tuesday, January 24, 2023 at 6:30 p.m.

DATE:  January 24, 2023

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2023 Draft Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the draft Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
Commission and is intended for the 2023 calendar year.

Purpose of the Commission
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.

Scope of the Commission
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission and outline
the areas of focus for the remainder of 2023. It includes proposed programs and projects
that will be implemented and completed throughout the year, some of which may extend
beyond 2023. Some of the items have carried over from the 2022 workplan.

DRAFT 2023 WORKPLAN
The 2023 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission has
identified as key areas of interest in furtherance of its purpose. The following list of ideas,
